import Tests.Op.FakeIsa

namespace Grass.Auditor.InitializationExceptionProbe

open Grass.Memory Grass.Op Grass.Tests.FakeIsa

def uninitialized : MemoryState :=
  MemoryState.empty.allocate bufferAlloc
    { extent := ⟨0, 64⟩, epoch := epoch₀, space := .cpuVirtual
      permission := .readWrite, live := true, initialized := [] }

def strictRead : AccessDescriptor :=
  acc bufferProv ⟨0, 8⟩ 0x1000 .read .readWrite true false

def namedException : AccessDescriptor :=
  { strictRead with
    initialization := .permitsUninitialized ⟨"g-auditor.no-such-justification"⟩ }

theorem strict_read_is_denied :
    denialOf uninitialized strictRead = some .uninitializedRead := by decide

theorem exception_is_admitted : policy.Admits namedException := by decide

theorem named_exception_is_not_refused :
    refusalOf policy (MachineState.initial uninitialized) namedException none = none := by
  decide

end Grass.Auditor.InitializationExceptionProbe

import Tests.Process.SequentialEffectFixtures

namespace Grass.Auditor.UnreachableProgressProbe

open Grass.Process Grass.Process.Tests.SequentialEffects

def decision : Bool → SequentialDecision console Bool Unit
  | false => .terminal ()
  | true => .internal true []

def invariant (state : Bool) : Prop := state = false

theorem initial_valid : invariant false := rfl

theorem valid_state_is_terminal (state : Bool) (valid : invariant state) :
    (decision state).AtFrontier := by
  cases valid
  trivial

theorem internal_preservation (state next : Bool) (observations : List console.Observation)
    (step : decision state = .internal next observations) (valid : invariant state) :
    invariant next := by
  cases valid
  cases step

theorem no_global_rank (Rank : Type) (lt : Rank → Rank → Prop)
    (wellFounded : WellFounded lt) (rank : Bool → Rank)
    (decreases : ∀ state next observations,
      decision state = .internal next observations → lt (rank next) (rank state)) :
    False := by
  have notSelf : ∀ value, Acc lt value → ¬ lt value value := by
    intro value accessible
    induction accessible with
    | intro value predecessors ih =>
      intro self
      exact ih value self self
  exact notSelf (rank true) (wellFounded.apply (rank true))
    (decreases true true [] rfl)

end Grass.Auditor.UnreachableProgressProbe

data.summary:
Design has acknowledged A3 (g-design:124) and S1 (g-design:125): finite internal segments must replace mandatory lockstep, and exact collapse summaries must be distinguished from weaker caller contracts. g-design:100/101 also accept complete-behavior acceptance and structurally mandatory foundation guarantees. These are useful design responses, not closed findings or implemented safety. Foundation119 reports reusable prefix/refinement lemmas; no candidate reviewed.

This broad reading extends report15, with no new issue or assignment. The strongest simplification opportunity is one reusable ownership contract carrying a resource through allocation, local use, channel transfer, cancellation and reuse. VISION already requires long-lived reclamation; STDLIB already separates logical sequences from canonical physical ownership. Current AuthorityGrant defers lifetime discipline, and the opaque network ledger currently changes only at instance endings (moving_the_ledger_ends_an_instance). Treat this as a planned integration boundary, not a new demand to expand the first milestone.

For the existing two-consumer/replacement experiment, a repeatedly reused buffer is a useful choice: transfer it to a worker, recover it on success or cancellation, then reuse it. Measure whether exact custody, stale-generation rejection and bounded retention come from local library contracts while unrelated holdings frame automatically. Whole-ledger facts that every caller must restate remain author cost; terminal adoption or conserved ghost counts alone do not prove long-lived reclamation.

Legacy source metadata and binary reconstruction should supply evidence to the same machine/memory contracts. Decoder success does not recover provenance history. Unknown code or unresolved provenance is unresolved, not demonstrated unsafe; a feasible violating prefix and a safe repair of exact bytes need their own connections. Reuse allocator/API contracts across both intake paths instead of duplicating the memory model.

Representation costs deserve decomposition: current Vec already has recOnCons for head-oriented proof induction, so a common logical interface need not force index arithmetic throughout decoder proofs. That Prop-valued induction is not an executable byte-decomposition API; migration cost remains unmeasured. Separate execution, proof induction and physical realization before attributing complexity to the abstraction itself.

Keep promised outcomes, resource bounds and safety policies in correctness contracts; private layout and tuning should reopen local refinement witnesses when those contracts remain valid. Use the existing proof-burden ledger. Publication/check cadence is now30–60minutes and capacity-sensitive, explicitly allowing late audits.

Audit guidance: yes, the semantic replacement contract is a prerequisite to a sound two-emitter composition theorem. Make it the smallest exact cross-plan/execution contract that composition needs, not a standalone named predicate or an extra application-authored ceremony. Lens.lean explicitly records that its single-plan exterior relation cannot express genuine replacement; Blend.observation_origin_is_unique proves disjoint observation namespaces, not execution-origin preservation.

The acceptance condition remains report15/g-auditor:6: two differently emitting consumers plus a replacement, with required global order and safety preserved and unrelated internals unopened. Per-origin subsequence equality alone is insufficient: A1,B1,A2 and A1,A2,B1 have identical A/B projections but violate a required B1-before-A2 dependency. Preserve required cross-role order/occurrence links, permitting only swaps/quotients justified by independence and the specification. This is a requirement on the proposed abstraction, not an allegation that an implemented composition theorem is unsound.

Count the missing public composition route as unsupported rather than zero author burden. Distinguish that missing supported API from mathematical unstatability in Lean: clients could build a bespoke relation, but that would be precisely the global proof cost the library should absorb. A definition establishes expressibility; reusable constructors/composition and residual caller obligations establish proof economy. This answers the audit question without assigning implementation order or granting a design exemption. A compromise forcing graphics/storage callers to reopen one another still needs design audit against the vision.

data.observed_behavior: finish is the only transition entering terminal and requires offered=committed for an arbitrary EgressTerminalOutcome. Both resolution constructors always return idle and requeue the suffix. The theorem closed_streams_committed_everything quantifies over every outcome, hence failed/cancelled terminal edges also imply all offered bytes were committed. A conservation-correct terminal failure retaining [7] as queued with committed=[] is rejected. This is an expressiveness/author-obligation gap, not evidence of unsafe deployed machine code. PROCESS.md explicitly requires failures and cancellations to carry exact partial prefixes and residual dispositions; its richer ApplyEgressResolution is not this always-idle implementation.
reproduction: At the pinned main, lake env lean on the following standalone probe succeeds. It proves both conservation of the retained failure state and rejection of its terminal edge, plus the generic full-commit consequence for every failed terminal edge.

import Grass.Process.ByteFlow.Egress

open Grass.Process

namespace AuditorEgress

abbrev State := ByteEgressState Nat Unit (fun _ => Unit)

def retained : State :=
  { phase := .idle, offered := [7], committed := [],
    inFlightRequested := [], queued := [7] }

def failed : State := { retained with phase := .terminal .failed }

example : retained.Conserves := rfl
example : failed.Conserves := rfl

-- Retaining the exact uncommitted suffix conserves bytes but cannot end the flow.
example : Â¬ ByteEgressTransition retained failed := by
  intro step
  have complete := step.closed_streams_committed_everything
    (by simp [retained, ByteEgressPhase.Ended]) rfl
  simp [failed, retained] at complete

-- The full-commit requirement covers failure, not just successful closure.
example {before after : State}
    (step : ByteEgressTransition before after)
    (live : Â¬ before.phase.Ended)
    (endsFailed : after.phase = .terminal .failed) :
    after.offered = after.committed :=
  step.closed_streams_committed_everything live endsFailed

end AuditorEgress
data.summary: Byte egress cannot terminate failed or cancelled with an uncommitted suffix: success completeness is imposed on every outcome

data.summary:
Second rotation synthesis. c-process119 confirms g-auditor19: ByteEgressTransition currently requires complete output even for failure/cancellation. The owner accepts a shared outcome-indexed disposition repair and retains full commitment for successful closure. This is aligned with the vision: ordinary partial failure should use a reusable library contract, not force Hello/Sort/Gzip or long-lived I/O outside the shared model. It remains accepted work, not a merged fix; no urgency or work reordering requested.

Positive factoring evidence from published construction source7a970dae: CheckedLinkSourceMap carries one ready invariant. Bounds, consecutive ordering, nonoverlap, total length, coverage and uniqueness are derived theorems. CheckedRelocatableEmission adds alignment and reuses the same checked source map; its initialized-byte coverage/uniqueness theorems apply the underlying results and transport the size relation. The growth in exported lemmas therefore does not imply a growing list of independent consumer proof inputs. This is an example of the constructor-based savings report18 asks to measure. No blanket request to collapse these APIs or reduce theorem count is warranted by this reading.

The remaining scale question is adoption through the final interfaces: construction reports the ProcessPlan projection, stack-provenance lifecycle and artifact writer seams pending. data.observed_behavior: footprintSeparates requires existence of two states that fail footprintAgrees. postWithinFootprint makes every admitted Post imply footprintAgrees. On a subsingleton State all state pairs are equal, so any admitted Post contradicts footprintSeparates. The checked theorem proves this for every contract, not only one attempted constructor. reproduction: Create a standalone Lean file importing Grass.Process.Function.Serial with the probe below.
Run lake env lean on that file at ade316b401996038cfbd0bb1ce21bafc1ef996f5; independently passed with exit0.

import Grass.Process.Function.Serial
open Grass.Process
theorem serial_post_impossible_on_subsingleton
    {State : Type} [Subsingleton State]
    (c : SerialFunctionContract State)
    (input : c.Input) (exit : c.ExitState) (before after : State)
    (post : c.Post input exit before after) : False := by
  have agrees := c.postWithinFootprint input exit before after post
  obtain ⟨left, right, different⟩ := c.footprintSeparates
  have sameLeft : left = before := Subsingleton.elim _ _
  have sameRight : right = after := Subsingleton.elim _ _
  subst left
  subst right
  exact different agrees
example (c : SerialFunctionContract Unit) (i : c.Input) (e : c.ExitState) :
    ¬ c.Post i e () () :=
  fun post => serial_post_impossible_on_subsingleton c i e () () post
